checks: The span condition provides real a_i with the exact cancellation equation. For finite I, small signed t keeps all row scale factors positive. Only the selected strictly positive rows receive additive perturbations, so positivity is maintained there and all other supports stay fixed.
The column-sum vector changes by t times the cancellation equation and hence stays exactly equal to one. Feasibility of the rescaled row argument follows by dividing by its positive factor.

Each projective parameter s_i=t/(1+t a_i) has s_i=t+O(t²) and (1+t a_i)s_i=t exactly. Selected rows contribute the stated remainder plus the baseline scaling term and tℓ_i. The unselected active rows contribute only their affine scaling terms.

The sum of remainders is o(|t|) and the two signs of feasible t force the remaining linear coefficient to vanish. This yields an exact equality for all small signed t, including the empty selected set.

For a single selected row the inverse map is t=s_r/(1−a_r s_r) near zero, and the positive scale and positive weight preserve the sign of the capacity remainder. Dividing a second-order expansion by s_r²/2 yields Q ≤ 0.

Archived sources f62fe2e83b180bf3 §3 and 58f8bbb67f63ee23 §1 supply respectively the exact one-row identity and the simultaneous scaling argument. The frozen two-sided directional derivative assumption is sufficient for the joint remainder identity. Both archived raw digests match the frozen provenance.

overlap.comparison: The accepted full-cut exclusion uses a particular two-row coordinate transfer and a one-sided derivative jump. It does not give the simultaneous proportional compensation identity for selected row directions with sum in the active span.

readability: The capacity specialization uses φ as a shorthand for the chosen row capacity. The proof only uses the stated equality f_r=ω_r φ and the directional derivative hypothesis.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: An exact projective rescaling isolates the selected rows’ tangent remainders along a feasible two-sided line, with only directional differentiability on those rows.
